name: Trusted Execution Environments
description: TEEs and enclaves (Intel SGX, ARM TrustZone, TDX, SEV), attestation, and confidential computing.
narrative:
Early USENIX Security work asked whether Intel SGX could be trusted and answered no: Foreshadow (2018) extracted enclave attestation keys via transient execution, The Guard Dilemma (2018) turned enclave code against its owner, and A Bad Dream (2018) attacked TPMs. Building then advanced alongside breaking: VRASED (2019) verified remote attestation, TeeRex (2020) and PARTEMU (2020) exposed SGX and TrustZone trusted code, and Visor (2020) brought TEEs to the cloud.

CIPHERLEAKS (2021) opened the AMD SEV ciphertext side channel and VoltPillager (2021) added faults, while ReZone (2022) and SGXFuzz (2022) pushed privilege reduction and fuzzing. By 2023-2024 the frontier moved to confidential VMs and ARM CCA: AEX-Notify (2023) stopped single-stepping, SHELTER (2023) extended CCA, and HECKLER (2024) and CacheWarp (2024) broke AMD SEV confidential VMs.

milestones.title: Foreshadow: Extracting the Keys to the Intel SGX Kingdom with Transient Out-of-Order Execution
